# Independent source review — GROUND-CLEARANCE-R01v1 / ADR 0185

**VERDICT: ACCEPT for the parent's full regression, static checks and exact-head CI.** No must-fix defect found in the changed sources. Findings below are advisories and evidence-hygiene items; none of them justify widening this bounded repair.

## Scope actually reviewed (exact source)

Read in full and cross-checked against `final-candidate.patch`: `godot/scripts/core/movement.gd`, `godot/scripts/core/navigation.gd`, `godot/test/fixtures/synthetic_ground_movement.gd`, `godot/test/test_movement_clearance.gd`, `godot/test/ground_clearance_focus.gd`, `godot/test/test_movement.gd`, `godot/test/test_movement_readmission.gd`; plus the collaborators the gate depends on for reasoning only (`int_math.gd`, `spatial_world.gd`, `transforms.gd`, `test/framework/test_case.gd`, `test/run_tests.gd`), the contract, ADR 0185 and the four evidence JSONs.

I ran nothing. Every runtime statement below is either (a) a reading of source, explicitly marked as such, or (b) a citation of the supplied evidence files. The patch content matches the current full sources for all seven files, so the two are consistent and I reviewed the sources as authoritative.

## 1. Correctness of the admission gate

**Gate ordering — correct.** `_refuse_admission()` now reads: `_refuse_profile_terms` (profile id → life stage → mode range → mode profiled → species → load sign → load capacity) → `_refuse_contact_terms` (bound → live owner → location current) → `_navigation.is_ready` → **new `_refuse_clearance`** → `_route_ends_at` → `_refuse_route_start`. That is exactly the contract's "immediately after request readiness and before route-end/start checks". Every earlier gate keeps its prior precedence; nothing was reordered.

**Actual qualification, not a default — correct.** `_refuse_clearance()` calls `profile_clearance_class_into(admission.profile_id, _scratch)` on `self`. GDScript method dispatch is virtual, so this resolves to the fixture's override under test and to the unmodified production implementation otherwise — which is precisely why the fixture can exercise real `begin_travel()` without a production seam. Production `profile_clearance_class_into()` is byte-unchanged and still returns `out.refuse(REFUSE_PROFILE_CLEARANCE)` for every one of the four published starter profiles; its named error is propagated (`return StringName(_scratch.error)`) rather than converted into a class. No default, no clamp, no fallback.

**Exact descriptor class — correct.** `_scratch.value` is captured into the local `profile_class` *before* the second `_into` call overwrites the shared scratch, satisfying `int_math.gd`'s documented aliasing rule. The comparison is `!=` on the actual `_d_clearance[_r_route_id[row]]` value — strict equality, no monotonicity or "larger class also fits" assumption. `REFUSE_ROUTE_CLEARANCE` carries the contract's exact string `ROUTE_PROFILE_CLEARANCE_MISMATCH`.

**Scratch safety downstream — correct.** After `_refuse_clearance` returns `REFUSE_NONE`, `_route_ends_at()`, `_refuse_route_start()` and `begin_travel()`'s own `route_cell_into()` each re-derive from `_scratch` immediately; no caller holds a stale `_scratch` value across the new calls.

**Refusal before any attachment — correct, and this is the safety-critical property.** All new refusals return out of `_refuse_admission()`, which `begin_travel()` consumes *before* `_attach_route()` is reached. The re-admission bookkeeping that could corrupt an existing traveller — `if _movement_phase[row] == MOTION_TRAVELLING: _travelling_count -= 1`, `_reset_motion(row)`, cursor/admission writes, `_navigation.route_generation_of(...)` — all live inside `_attach_route()` and are therefore unreachable on a clearance refusal. I traced this specifically for the packed columns that have no public reader (`_vx/_vz`, `_next_x/_next_z`, `_grid_cell/_grid_next`, `_cursor_route_generation`): none is written on any refusing path. Navigation route ownership is likewise untouched — the new gate takes no reference, and `_hold_route()` is only called from `_attach_route()`.

**No production widening.** Verified by reading the whole of both changed production files: no new test flag, override parameter, constructor option, permissive default, alternate public admission entry point, packed column, runtime catalog, schema bump or mutable profile authority. No production source references the test fixture. `ROUTE_SEMANTICS_VERSION` is unchanged (2), `_d_clearance` is an existing descriptor column whose meaning and width are unchanged, no route geometry / PATH-R02 semantics / retained-remainder / cost / reserved-field / saved-column validator (`Movement.columns_refusal`, `Transforms.columns_refusal`, `SpatialWorld` §1 block) is touched. No body dimension, profile, contact producer, footprint, mode, turn, support or lease value is introduced anywhere — consistent with ADR 0185's explicit exclusion list. No memory-ledger delta is owed, because no new packed column exists.

## 2. The ready-route getter

`Navigation.route_clearance_into(row, out)` is a faithful sibling of `route_length_into()`: `is_ready(row)` is the sole admission test, and `request_phase()` already clamps `row < 0 || row >= PATH_REQUEST_CAPACITY` to `PHASE_FREE`, so invalid, free, queued, mid-search, cancelled, stale and blocked rows all take the `REFUSE_NOT_READY` branch without indexing anything. `out.refuse()` zeroes `.value` and sets `.error`, so an ignored return cannot surface a plausible class.

**Read-only — confirmed by source, not only by test.** The success path touches exactly two things: `_last_refusal` and `out`. It does **not** refresh `_d_use_low/_d_use_high`, so repeated reads cannot perturb `_lowest_use_unreferenced()` eviction order; it does not touch `_d_refcount`, `_d_generation`, `_r_phase`, `_r_route_id`, the queue links or the arena. This matters more than the test can prove, because last-use tick has no public accessor.

**Diagnostic clearing.** The success path sets `_last_refusal = REFUSE_NONE`, which the contract required and which `route_length_into()`/`route_cell_into()` notably do **not** do. This is a deliberate, contract-mandated local divergence from its siblings, and it is documented in the function's own docstring as repair a2. I flag the asymmetry only so a later reader does not "harmonise" it in either direction without checking the contract. (LOW)

## 3. Test-boundary discipline

The fixture `test/fixtures/synthetic_ground_movement.gd` overrides exactly one method, `profile_clearance_class_into()`, and adds one test-only configurator. It does **not** override `begin_travel()`, `_refuse_admission()`, `_refuse_clearance()`, `_attach_route()` or any other gate — so every clearance test drives the real production admission path, ordering and attachment. Invalid profile ids fall through `is_profile()` to the parent's `REFUSE_PROFILE_ID`, i.e. the override substitutes only the one missing envelope value and never the identity check preceding it. It declares no `_init`, inheriting the parent's five-argument constructor, so all real collaborators are preserved. It is not discoverable as a suite (`run_tests._discover_suites()` reads only files directly under `res://test` whose names begin `test_`), so it cannot be executed as tests by accident.

`ground_clearance_focus.gd` inherits `run_tests.gd` and overrides only `_discover_suites()`. Because the inherited supervisor re-executes `(get_script() as Script).resource_path`, the worker re-runs the focus script, so the override applies to the worker as well as the supervisor — the three-suite selection is real, not silently replaced by full discovery. No runner logic is copied, and the new suite inherits no legacy tests.

**Base-production refusal remains independently covered, twice.** `test_movement.gd::test_no_profile_publishes_a_clearance_class` was rewritten to construct a *separate* production `MovementScript` and assert against it, with its expectations unweakened (all four profiles → `REFUSE_PROFILE_CLEARANCE`; `-1` → `REFUSE_PROFILE_ID`). Independently, `test_movement_clearance.gd::test_production_movement_refuses_a_ready_class_one_route_for_every_starter_species` drives real production `begin_travel()` for mouse/mole/otter/squirrel on genuinely READY class-1 routes with live contacts and asserts `PROFILE_CLEARANCE_UNSPECIFIED`, `MOTION_IDLE`, full snapshot equality and byte-identical `Transforms.state_bytes()`. Neither is pointed at the fixture.

**Reference-movement labelling** is present in both amended suite headers and in `_build()`'s docstring, and correctly declines to call the fixture's passing motion "qualified physical travel".

## 4. Preservation of prior coverage

Diffing the two amended suites: the only changes are the fixture preload, the `_build()` instantiation line plus docstring, the two header paragraphs, and the one production-instance rewrite in `test_no_profile_publishes_a_clearance_class`. **No prior test, scenario, assertion or expectation is deleted, skipped or weakened.** That matters substantively here, because the precise integration checks that the clearance gate could have silently broken — the 30-tick exact-cap run, the 109-unit first tick with remainder 98, the 90-tick zero-drift run, ford height traversal, successor-row ownership, off-map settle, speed-equivalence at 1x/2x/4x, invisible-view independence, the twelve-starter cohort, load boundaries, profile/contact staleness, and the whole readmission travelling-count suite — now all execute *through* the new gate rather than around it.

## 5. Required witnesses — coverage assessment

| Witness | Status |
|---|---|
| Production refusal, four species, no state/count/route-ownership change | Covered, with full public snapshot + `state_bytes()` + `travelling_count()` |
| Synthetic class 1 admits real class 1, class 2 admits class 2, with actual advancement | Covered; asserts post-tick X changed, not merely `true` |
| Both mismatch directions (1/2 and 2/1) refuse by name, idle preserved | Covered, each with full snapshot + `state_bytes()` |
| Mid-travel mismatched re-admission preserves everything, then restored class continues | Covered: 15 public getters, travelling count, `authoritative_digest()`, `state_bytes()`, route id/generation/refcount, then `advance_tick(2)` proves the **original** journey resumes (`MOTION_TRAVELLING`, X moved) |
| Getter reports 1 and 2; refuses invalid/free/pending/cancelled/stale-after-service; prepopulated result zeroed; success clears `last_refusal`; identity/refcount/generation unchanged | Covered |
| Refusal priority: earlier gates win; clearance precedes route-end **and** route-start | Covered (unready, life-stage mismatch, invalid profile id, unbound contact; then wrong-end and wrong-start both yielding `ROUTE_PROFILE_CLEARANCE_MISMATCH`) |
| No private mutable accessor added for tests | Confirmed — every snapshot value comes from a pre-existing public reader |

## 6. Counterfactual evidence (as supplied, not re-run)

`mutation-results.json` declares the three contract-named mutants against the exact control source hashes, with `script_or_engine_error: false` for each and non-zero failure counts distinct from the control (71/2655/0):

- `qualification-bypass` (propagated refusal → `REFUSE_NONE`): 1 failure, caught by the production four-species test. This is the mutant that proves the qualification result is *consulted*, not merely read.
- `mismatch-bypass`: 5 failures across both mismatch directions, the readmission test and both ordering tests.
- `getter-fixed-class-one` (`_d_clearance[...]` → literal `1`): 5 failures, proving the descriptor's *actual* class is read rather than a constant, and that the class-2 positive path is genuinely class-2.

Each mutant is killed by at least one witness that a weaker suite would have missed. I did not execute these; I verified only that the declared `old`/`new` snippets correspond to real statements in the current sources and that the claimed failing test names exist in the reviewed suites.

## 7. Findings

**MEDIUM — latent: empty-error propagation would admit.** `_refuse_clearance()` returns `StringName(_scratch.error)`; `REFUSE_NONE` is the empty name, and `_refuse_admission()`'s caller treats `REFUSE_NONE` as pass. No production or in-repo path can produce `false` with an empty `.error` (`IntResult.refuse()` is always called with a non-empty constant, and `profile_clearance_class_into()` has exactly two refusal constants), so this is not a live defect and no counterexample exists today. It is a shape worth hardening later — a future override or refactor that refused with an empty string would be admitted rather than refused. Suggested (not required for this repair): `var code := StringName(_scratch.error); return code if code != REFUSE_NONE else REFUSE_PROFILE_CLEARANCE`.

**LOW — documented-unreachable branch / equivalent mutant.** The `route_clearance_into` failure path inside `_refuse_clearance` cannot be reached, because `is_ready(row)` was just asserted and nothing between the two calls mutates navigation. The docstring says so, which is the right treatment; this repo's convention (`_height_at_into`, `_allocate_cursors`) is to also record such an equivalent mutant explicitly in the decision record. Worth one line in 0185's follow-up rather than a source change.

**LOW — scope boundary worth naming: clearance is admission-time only.** `_advance_row()` revalidates route validity, cursor ownership and admitted profile *revision*, but not clearance class. Changing a clearance answer mid-journey without re-admission therefore does not settle the body. This is correct for this bounded repair (no per-tick clearance revalidation is contracted, and there is no clearance-revision concept to hang one on), and the readmission test never ticks while mismatched, so the behaviour is simply unspecified rather than wrong. Recommend one sentence in `movement.gd`'s header or ADR 0185 stating it, so a later reader does not mistake the silence for an oversight.

**LOW — getter test assertion completeness.** The free-row case asserts only `value == 0` (not `last_refusal`), and the pending/cancelled/stale cases assert `ok`/`value`/`last_refusal` but not `_result.error`. The invalid-row case does assert `.error`, so the error channel is covered once. Non-blocking.

**LOW — style.** `test_the_getter_reports_the_readied_class_and_refuses_every_non_ready_phase()` runs well past CLAUDE.md's 30-line guidance; `test_a_mismatched_readmission_mid_travel...` likewise. Both are cohesive single scenarios and splitting them would fragment the before/after witness, so I would not change them, but the deviation is real. Also, `test_the_clearance_gate_is_ordered_after_earlier_gates_and_before_route_end_start()` uses `_residents.spawn_with_stage(...).ref` without first asserting `.ok`; every other spawn in these suites checks it. A one-line `assert_true(spawned.ok, ...)` would make a future failure there diagnosable instead of a bare script error.

**EVIDENCE HYGIENE — `patch-normalization.json` is stale relative to the final candidate.** Its `final_sha256` block records `godot/scripts/core/navigation.gd = 4f662c44…` and `godot/test/test_movement_clearance.gd = c5706f82…`, whereas the manifest and `focus-a2.json` both carry `27356d8d…` and `78fda596…` for those two files. The other five files agree exactly. That divergence is confined precisely to the two files touched by the repair-a2 diagnostic fix (the getter's `_last_refusal = REFUSE_NONE` and its corresponding assertions), so the chain is coherent rather than contradictory — the normalization record simply describes the pre-a2 application. It should say so explicitly, or be re-emitted against the final sources; otherwise a later reader will reasonably read it as a hash mismatch between the patch record and the shipped source. `final-candidate.patch` itself does contain the a2 change and does match the current sources, so no source ambiguity exists.

**FOR THE PARENT'S REGRESSION — not a source defect, but the one thing this scope cannot settle.** This change makes production `Movement.begin_travel()` refuse **unconditionally**, for every caller, because no starter profile qualifies. That is the intended and correct consequence of binding admission to the existing boundary, and ADR 0185 accepts it. But the supplied scope contains only three suites; any other in-repo production caller of `begin_travel()` (job assignment, settlement wiring, an integration or save/restore suite) that previously relied on admission succeeding will now fail. The focus run's 71 tests / 2655 assertions / 0 failures is evidence for these three suites only. The parent's full regression is the gate that must confirm no other caller or suite is silently broken; I cannot and do not assert that from this packet.

## 8. Explicitly out of scope, and correctly so

No actual clearance profiles, body/gear envelopes, posture, physical contacts, footprint offsets, additional traversal modes, turn or support costs, reservation leases, source-bound sweeps, safe topology, expanded-graph Dijkstra comparison, whole-save milestone or release acceptance are intended by this repair, and their absence is not a defect here. The pre-existing open items visible in the reviewed files — the 12,384-byte architecture ledger arrears, the blocked `_profile_life_stage:B8[4]` packed column, `REFUSE_CONTACT_REVISION` being declared but unused in `_refuse_contact_terms`, `test_movement_readmission.gd::after_each` nulling the static `_shared_world`, and `route_length_into`/`route_cell_into` not clearing `last_refusal` on success — are all unchanged pre-existing conditions. I record them as separate items for their own owners; none of them justifies widening this repair, and none blocks acceptance.

No first-playable, performance, native-memory or physical-travel-qualification claim is made or supported by this change.
